title: autotune: smarter defaults for batching/caching, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We observe significant per-token cost variance across customers due to conservative defaults for batching and KV caching and a lack of guided quantization profiles. This PR implements an autotune path that picks safer but cost-effective defaults for batching/caching, introduces model-aware quantization profile heuristics, and adds a first-pass unit-economics (unit-econ) tooling surface to estimate per-request cost impact.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces an autotune controller that recommends and applies default batching and prefix/KV cache policies based on observed sequence length distributions and tail latency SLOs.
- Adds quantization profile heuristics that prefer int8/4bit variants for compatible models and workload patterns, with automatic quality regression gating.
- Implements a unit-econ CLI and internal API that projects per-request token cost and expected savings from changing batching/caching/quant profiles.
- Provides telemetry hooks and a perf-canary job to validate throughput/latency regressions before rollout.

Implementation notes:
- Autotune controller lives under runtime/autotune and runs as a low-priority background reconciler. It consumes sequence length histograms and SLO configs from the control plane. Recommendations are surfaced to the Console and can be auto-applied per-customer if their policy allows.
- Quant profiles are modeled as lightweight metadata (profiles/*) and matched to models via a fingerprint heuristic. Each profile includes a fallback path to full precision and an evaluation prompt set for regression checks.
- Unit-econ tooling (tools/unit_econ) exposes an estimate endpoint and a CLI that takes a sample workload and outputs projected cost delta by changing parameters. It uses the same cost model as billing but in a read-only, non-billable mode.

Risk and mitigation:
- Quality regressions from quantization: every quant profile application is gated behind a regression test that runs a small prompt set in the staging canary and compares embedding/text similarity and token-level perplexity thresholds. If a regression is detected, the controller marks the profile as not-applicable for that model+workload.
- Latency regressions from batching: autotune uses a multi-objective scoring function that weighs cost savings vs P99 latency impact and will decline configurations that violate latency SLOs.

Testing:
- Unit tests for controller heuristics and profile matching (runtime/autotune/*_test.go).
- Integration tests running a perf-canary (perf-canary/workflows/autotune-run) that exercises both batching and quantization paths against a representative Llama-variant and a GPT-style model.
- Manual canary rollout to 5 internal customers to validate unit-econ projections vs observed billing.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge and deploy controller in shadow mode (recommendations only) for 2 weeks.
2) Run perf-canary and validate no >2% regression in throughput or >5ms p99 delta across sampled workloads.
3) Enable opt-in auto-apply for internal customers, monitor unit-econ accuracy.
4) Gradual enable by segment with Console toggle.

Related: Linear ENG-3245 (autotune defaults), ENG-3310 (unit-econ tooling). References to docs and prior PRs: see pr-51023, pr-50321 for earlier autotune iterations.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add autotune controller code and tests
- [x] Add quant profile heuristics + regression gating
- [x] Add unit-econ CLI + API
- [x] Perf-canary linked job
- [x] Console UI hooks (recommendation surface)

Notes for reviewers: look at runtime/autotune/controller.go for the scoring function and tools/unit_econ/README.md for the model used in projections. The autotune controller is intentionally conservative; parameter weights are configurable via feature flags.

release_notes: Introduce autotune controller for batching/caching defaults, model-aware quantization profile heuristics, and unit-econ tooling to estimate per-request cost impact. Default behavior is conservative and initially deployed in shadow mode. Customers can opt-in to auto-apply recommendations. Expected outcome: ~10-25% cost savings for workloads with high variability in sequence length.
